title: Enhancement: [sflow] Add acceptable range to incorrect number of samples error log
author: anders-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Low

### Description of the enhancement

In the sflow PTF script, the error message when an unexpected number of sample counts is received does not include the expected range: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/4082f1c4ed254713508e2908dc3a84c74a81b6af/ansible/roles/test/files/ptftests/py3/sflow_test.py#L249
It would be helpful if the range was included in the error so that the operator can see at a glance what the issue was (not enough samples, too many samples, etc).

### Current Behavior

Logs look like:
```
Expected Number of samples are not collected from Interface Ethernet192 in collector collector0 , Received 5
```

### Proposed Behavior

Logs would look like:
```
Expected Number of samples are not collected from Interface Ethernet192 in collector collector0 , Received 5 which is outside the acceptable range of 60 to 140
```

comments.author: anders-nexthop
comments.body:
> Some minor improvement opportunities:
> 
> * define 100 as a variable to be used consistently in sending and checking places.
> * fix the variable name pktlen -> pktcnt or alike.

I added NUM_SAMPLES/MIN_EXPECTED_SAMPLES/MAX_EXPECTED_SAMPLES as variables and applied them everywhere.

`pktlen` is actually already correct, as it defines the packet length sent for each round of packets. The script varies the length to make sure packets of different lengths are accounted for correctly. The choice of 100 as the pktlen is unfortunate, but after using variables for the expected number of samples it's not as confusing and so it's probably okay to leave it.
